newsitem.title: UK: NZ SPORT - Riegler to debut as TV presenter.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Riegler to debut as TV presenter.

text.p: LONDON, Dec 16 - A hit on the ski slopes, New Zealand's Claudia Riegler is set to make a name for herself off them next month when she makes her debut as a television presenter.

The 20-year-old, winner of the opening World Cup slalom of the season in Park City, Utah last month, has been asked to help front children's programme Confetti on Austrian television for five shows next month.
"It's good and something different for me," Riegler told NZPA during a break from training near Vienna.
"I don't know how it will go but I'm looking forward to it."
Riegler is no stranger to the media but her profile in Europe is growing in line with her skiing success.

Fluent in English, German, French and learning Italian, Riegler had a stint behind the microphone with pan-European channel Eurosport after she won the first World Cup race of her career at Serre Chevalier, France, in January.
She is in constant media demand in Austria, but appearing as a television presenter opens new doors.
Riegler, though, has her mind this week firmly fixed on the opening European leg of the World Cup slalom calendar at Crans Montana, Switzerland, on Saturday.
Her win in the United States, which puts her on top of the World Cup slalom standings, marks her as one of the racers to beat this year.
No longer the new kid on the block, the Austrian-based Riegler feels more comfortable in the company of her peers on the slopes this season.
"I think I'm more confident this season," Riegler said.
"Last year I was beginning from position 23, but this year I'm in the top seeding group, so that makes a difference.
"You know you can do it and compete with them."
Riegler had her confidence knocked a little this month, falling in two Europa Cup giant slalom races.
But her form in slalom is impeccable after taking a 0.07 second victory over world combined champion Pernilla Wiberg of Sweden at Park City.
Riegler said she was surprised at her victory.
"I was pretty sick and lost a lot of strength so I was surprised I went so well," she added.
"I had a really good first run, the second was a bit wild and I was behind, but I came through well.
"But I lost a lot of strength so I have been working hard on getting my strength back."
Part of that process has been coach Sepp Weissenbacher putting her through her paces on a steep, icy slope near Vienna.
"It was the steepest hill I've ever skied on," Riegler laughed.
"We went up there and there's like a sign that says 'Danger, don't ski here', and I said to Sepp 'Is that the hill?', and he said 'Yup, that's the hill!'
"It was hard but it was good fun."

The World Cup slalom leader after the opening race, Riegler is expecting her stiffest challenge this season to come from Wiberg, who has assumed the mantle of the leading all-round skier on the women's circuit.
"Pernilla will be hard to beat, but the Swiss are also going really well," Riegler said.
"It's hard to tell, they are all so good. It's just a matter of who is the most consistent."
Riegler's season will peak at the world championships in Sestrieres, Italy, in February, where she hopes to improve on her fourth placing from this year's event in Sierra Nevada, Spain.
